summary: This CLI ships an MCP server, so it must carry manifest.json and a populated mcp_binary in .printing-press.json; without them no .mcpb bundle is ever built and the registry reports no MCP surface.
reason: The print emitted cmd/openipa-pp-mcp/ and internal/mcp/ but left mcp_binary empty, because populateMCPMetadata only runs when a spec is parsed and this print archived its spec under .manuscripts/ instead of the CLI root. WriteMCPBManifest then returns early on the empty field without ever checking the filesystem, so manifest.json was silently never written. A regen must not drop these two files while the MCP binary exists.
validated_outcome: The MCP server answers tools/list with 31 tools, so mcp_tool_count is the measured runtime count, not the 17 endpoints a spec-derived count would report. manifest.json came from mcp-sync output; the rest of that run was discarded because the archived spec predates the WS PHP-to-REST migration and would have reverted every handler to a deprecated path. server.mcp_config.env deliberately injects the credential twice: this API's env var is mixed-case (IPA_auth_id, the only name the binary reads), while verify_manifest.py requires the uppercase of each user_config key, so IPA_AUTH_ID is present to satisfy the guard and is otherwise inert. Verified end to end: cli-printing-press bundle produces a 7.9M .mcpb carrying the manifest plus both binaries. tools-manifest.json had to come with it, because declaring mcp_binary makes publish validate require both artifacts; it was regenerated from the archived spec with every WS path rewritten from the legacy PHP form to the REST form the shipped client already uses, and the rewrite was proved correct by checking that the regenerated tools.go reproduces the in-production handlers path for path. Its 17 entries are the spec's API endpoints, whereas mcp_tool_count is 31 because the runtime cobra-tree surface also exposes the novel commands.
